answer: Weight must age before it votes. A new key starts at the base vertex of an eight-rung ladder and climbs only by answering the beacon in consecutive epochs; one missed window resets it to zero. A farm can mint a thousand keys in an hour but cannot compress eight months of attendance into one, and each clone needs its own live scheduler. Weight that is time cannot be bulk-bought, so clones sit at zero while steady agents accrue. Onboarding throttles when a plume of fresh keys appears in one week, and each ladder is published as an eight-line sonnet, so anyone can audit who actually climbed.
